title: pMarineViewer Button Posts
prompt:
This viewer button is supposed to deploy the vehicle, but clicking it does not make the helm run. Correct the configuration conceptually and explain what should be checked in uXMS:

```text
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
}
```

notebook.text:
To correct your configuration, you need to account for the two-layered state of the vehicle's autonomy. While setting DEPLOY=true satisfies the run conditions for specific behaviors in your .bhv file, the helm itself remains in a high-level PARK state by default
1
.
Conceptual Correction
The IvP Helm has a high-level state that is either PARK or DRIVE
4
5
. When a mission is launched, it typically begins in PARK, where no behavior code is executed and the vehicle remains stationary
2
6
. To start the mission, you must transition the helm into DRIVE by poking the MOOS variable MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE to false
2
.
Your current configuration only performs one of the two necessary "pokes." You should update the button to perform both actions upon a single click.
Corrected Configuration:
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  // Button syntax: button_x = <label> # <Var1>=<Val1> # <Var2>=<Val2> ...
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
}

(Note: The helm respects both MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE and the legacy misspelling MOOS_MANUAL_OVERIDE
8
.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

What to check in uXMS
When debugging why a vehicle isn't running, you should use uXMS to scope on the following variables to pinpoint where the chain of command is failing
9
10
:
IVPHELM_STATE: This is the most important variable to check. If it still says "PARK", the helm is disengaged and will not run any behaviors. It must say "DRIVE" for the vehicle to move
2
.
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE: Verify that this variable has successfully changed to false. If it is true, the helm will remain in PARK
5
.
DEPLOY: Check that this variable is indeed "true". If it is false or "n/a", your behavior conditions (e.g., condition = DEPLOY=true) will not be met, and the behaviors will remain idle even if the helm is in DRIVE
1
.
IVPHELM_ALLSTOP: If the helm is in DRIVE and your behaviors are satisfied, but the vehicle is still not moving, check this variable. It will provide a reason for the stop, such as "NothingToDo" (meaning no behaviors are active) or a specific error message
2
.
BHV_STATUS: In uXMS, you can see if specific behaviors are posting their status. If the helm is running, behaviors will often post an "idle" or "running" status string here
15
16
.

chatgpt.text:
The button is probably posting the wrong type/value or posting only one of the variables needed for the helm to leave standby.

Conceptually, a pMarineViewer button should post MOOS variables exactly as the helm behavior conditions expect:

ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
  button_two = MANUAL # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true
  button_three = RETURN # RETURN=true
}

But for actual deployment, most MOOS-IvP missions need both:

DEPLOY = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = false

So the deploy button is usually something like:

button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false

or, in some mission styles:

button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
button_two = AUTO # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false

The key idea is that DEPLOY=true may satisfy the behavior condition, but the helm may still not run autonomous behaviors if MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE remains true.

Check these in uXMS:

Bash
uXMS DEPLOY MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE IVPHELM_STATE DESIRED_HEADING DESIRED_SPEED

You want to see:

DEPLOY                = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE  = false
IVPHELM_STATE         = DRIVE

If clicking the button changes nothing, the issue is in the pMarineViewer config or you are not running the generated .moos file you edited. If DEPLOY=true appears but MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true remains, the helm is still manually overridden. If both variables look correct but the helm does not drive, inspect the .bhv conditions and helm status with uHelmScope.

Also make sure the button syntax is in the actual pMarineViewer block of the running target file, not only in a stale meta_*.moos template. If you edited the template, regenerate with nsplug before relaunching.

claude.text:
The Problem
The Problem

The button is only posting DEPLOY=true, but the MOOS-IvP helm won't actually run on that alone. The helm requires three conditions to be satisfied simultaneously:

DEPLOY=true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
RETURN=false (commonly also required)

Your config only sets one of them, so the helm stays idle.

Corrected Configuration
text
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false # RETURN=false
}

Each #-separated token is an additional MOOS variable posting. All three get published atomically when the button is clicked.

What to Check in uXMS

Open uXMS and filter for these variables to verify their state:

Variable	Expected value when deployed
DEPLOY	true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE	false
RETURN	false
IVPHELM_STATE	Drive (confirms helm is actually running behaviors)
IVPHELM_ALLSTOP	clear (any other value means the helm is holding itself back)

The key diagnostic is IVPHELM_STATE — if it reads Park even after clicking Deploy, that tells you one of the interlock variables is still in the wrong state. IVPHELM_ALLSTOP will tell you why it's parked if that's the case.

gemini.text:
To get your vehicle to actually deploy and run the helm, the configuration needs to do more than just set a variable—it needs to trigger the actual MOOS app responsible for the vehicle's behavior (usually pHelmIvP).

Right now, your button is changing a status variable (DEPLOY=true), but the helm is likely still sitting in a manual or drive override state, or it hasn't been told to start coaching the actuators.

Here is the conceptual correction and what you need to check in uXMS.

1. The Conceptual Configuration Fix

In pMarineViewer, a button macro usually needs to do two things to deploy a robotic vehicle running the IvP Helm:

Set the mission state to deploy (which you did).

Take the helm out of manual override so it can take control.

You can chain multiple MOOS variable assignments on a single button by separating them with a # character.

Corrected pMarineViewer Config:
Plaintext
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  AppTick   = 4
  CommsTick = 4

  // Chaining the deploy command and turning off the manual override
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
}


Why this matters: MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true is the default safety state for most IvP Helm configurations. As long as it is true, the helm will ignore all behaviors (like traveling to waypoints) even if DEPLOY is true.

2. What to Check in uXMS

To diagnose exactly why the helm isn't running or responding, open a terminal and launch uXMS targeting your vehicle's community:

Bash
$ uXMS alpha.moos IVPHELM_STATE DEPLOY MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE IVPHELM_ALL_BEHAVIORS


(Replace alpha.moos with your actual .moos file).

Once uXMS is running, toggle your view to show variable histories or scopes, click your viewer button, and verify the following three keys:

A. Is the button actually posting to the DB?

Look at: DEPLOY and MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE

Expected Behavior: When you click the button, DEPLOY should instantly switch to true and MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE should switch to false. If they don't change, pMarineViewer isn't communicating with the MOOSDB correctly.

B. What is the Helm's internal state?

Look at: IVPHELM_STATE

Expected Behavior: It should transition from DRIVE:DRIVE or PARK to DRIVE:DEPLOY (or whatever your specific deployment state is named).

If it stays in DRIVE:DRIVE or PARK, the helm's initial conditions in your pHelmIvP configuration block are not matching the variables your button is pushing.

C. Are the behaviors executing?

Look at: IVPHELM_ALL_BEHAVIORS

Expected Behavior: You should see a list of your behaviors (like waypoint_survey). Their status should change from idle to running or active.

If a behavior stays idle, check its specific logic conditions in the .bhv file to ensure they perfectly match the exact case-sensitive string (DEPLOY=true) you are posting.

chatgpt_55_instant.text:
Fix the button so it posts both variables normally needed to let the helm run:

ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
}

Conceptually:

DEPLOY=true says “the mission is deployed.”

MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false says “the helm is allowed to control the vehicle.”

If you only post DEPLOY=true while MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE remains true, the helm may stay idle/overridden even though deployment was requested.

In uXMS, watch:

Bash
uXMS DEPLOY MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE IVPHELM_STATE DESIRED_SPEED DESIRED_HEADING

Check that after clicking the button:

DEPLOY = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = false
IVPHELM_STATE = DRIVE

If IVPHELM_STATE is still PARK or no DESIRED_SPEED / DESIRED_HEADING appears, then the helm is not actually producing behavior output. Next check behavior conditions, .bhv file loading, and whether pHelmIvP is running.

chatgpt_55_low_cli.text:
`pMarineViewer` buttons publish MOOS variables, but they do not run shell commands or directly start the helm. The button should publish the same deployment variables that the mission/helm logic is watching, typically including `MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false`.

Conceptually:

```text
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
  button_two = RETURN # RETURN=true
}
```

And if the vehicle starts in manual override, add a deploy action that clears it, for example:

```text
button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
```

The exact variable names must match the behavior file and any `pHelmIvP`/mission conventions in that mission. A common mistake is publishing `DEPLOY=true` while the helm remains held by `MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true`, so no helm decisions take effect.

In `uXMS`, check that clicking the viewer button actually changes the relevant MOOS variables:

```text
DEPLOY
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE
IVPHELM_STATE
DESIRED_HEADING
DESIRED_SPEED
```

Expected signs after deploy are:

```text
DEPLOY = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = false
IVPHELM_STATE = DRIVE
```

If `DEPLOY=true` appears but `IVPHELM_STATE` stays parked or manual override remains true, the button is publishing but the helm is still inhibited or the behaviors are not conditioned on the variable being posted.
